system.name: UEP
system.one_liner: a portable CPU-proxy-based communication library for expert-parallel MoE workloads across GPUs and NICs

components.name: Proxy
components.role: CPU-side proxy thread that intercepts lightweight GPU control messages and issues token-level data communication on the GPU's behalf

components.name: Control buffer
components.role: temporarily buffers control messages (e.g. atomics) until their conditional check passes, then applies the carried values

components.name: FIFO
components.role: per-GPU queue over which GPU threads issue lightweight control messages to the CPU proxy

components.name: GPU 0
components.role: a GPU that initiates fine-grained token-level data movement by delegating transfers to the CPU proxy

components.name: GPU N
components.role: an additional GPU on the same node, delegating transfers the same way

components.name: Communication channel
components.role: a per-GPU ring buffer that temporarily buffers tokens to send in chunks; the high-throughput kernel uses several of these

flows.what: GPU threads issue lightweight control messages over PCIe to the CPU
the CPU proxy intercepts control messages from the FIFO
proxy issues token-level data communication on behalf of the GPU threads, buffered in per-GPU ring buffers
GPUDirect RDMA moves data payloads directly between Node 0's and Node 1's communication channels
atomic control messages (carried as immediate data) are buffered until their delivery condition is satisfied
manages / coordinates with the peer node's proxy

content.key_idea: UEP splits GPU-initiated communication into a token-level data path the GPU still drives, and a CPU-proxy control path that intercepts messages and enforces delivery semantics on the GPU's behalf, giving portability across GPUs/NICs without sacrificing performance.
content.reading_order: Two horizontal lanes, CPU above GPU, read left to right across two mirrored nodes connected by a GPUDirect RDMA link between their communication channels.

summary: UEP is a portable expert-parallel communication system for MoE workloads that splits work between GPUs and CPU proxies. Figure 5 shows this split as two lanes, CPU above and GPU below, mirrored across two nodes. On each node, GPUs issue lightweight control messages over PCIe into per-GPU FIFOs; a CPU Proxy intercepts these messages and issues the actual token-level data transfer on the GPU's behalf through per-GPU Communication channel ring buffers, which move data payloads to the peer node via GPUDirect RDMA. A separate Control buffer holds atomic control messages, carried as immediate data, until the condition they specify passes, at which point their values are applied; the two nodes' proxies also manage each other directly. The design lets the GPU keep fast, pipelined data movement while the CPU proxy absorbs NIC- and delivery-semantics complexity.
